newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * NATO's summit starting in Madrid on Tuesday will not be the end of Romania's efforts to join the Alliance, but a new start, said Radu Vasile, secretary general of the ruling National Peasant Party. Vasile said it was time for Romania to focus its efforts on domestic reforms.

* U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit to Romania -- scheduled for July 11 -- is the proof that Romania has acquired the status of a democratic country which cannot be excluded from the future architecture of Europe, Vasile said.

He said Clinton's visit should not be interpreted as a consolation for the U.S. decision to invite only Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to join NATO. The visit would guarantee American support for Romania's efforts to fulfil NATO membership criteria.

* The National Peasant Party considers that conflicts within the ruling coalition have been defused and that the alliance's members have preserved the minimum of confidence needed to continue cooperation within the coalition government. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
